heading: What they might still be able to do
lede: You cannot tell someone which of these applies to them — that is exactly the line. What you can do is know that these exist, so you understand why getting to a lawyer quickly matters, and so nobody walks away believing there is nothing left to try.

critical.title: Ask whether they ever travelled on a TPS travel document.
critical.body: This is the single question most likely to change someone's case. Many people who had TPS first entered the country without being inspected at a border post. That blocks them from applying for a green card from inside the United States, even if they marry a U.S. citizen. But since July 2022, a TPS holder who travelled abroad on Form I-512T and was let back in is treated as having been inspected and admitted. That one trip can turn an impossible case into a workable one.
critical.why: Ask it, write down the answer, and make sure the lawyer hears it. Do not try to work out what it means.

source.org: USCIS Policy Alert, TPS and Adjustment of Status

critical.title: Losing TPS does not automatically close off asylum.
critical.body: Asylum normally has to be filed within one year of arriving, and people who have been here a decade assume that door shut long ago. But the regulation lists holding TPS as an extraordinary circumstance that excuses a late filing, as long as they file within a reasonable period after it ends. Many people do not know this, and some are told the opposite.
critical.why: The word that matters is soon. A reasonable period is not measured in years.

paths.name: Asylum
paths.plain: For someone who fears persecution because of their race, religion, nationality, politics, or the group they belong to.

paths.name: A family petition
paths.plain: A U.S. citizen can petition a spouse, child, parent or sibling. A permanent resident can petition only a spouse or unmarried child. Spouses, minor children and parents of citizens skip the waiting line entirely.

paths.name: An employer petition
paths.plain: Usually requires an employer and a long labor certification process. A few categories let a person petition for themselves.

paths.name: U visa
paths.plain: For a victim of a serious crime who was harmed by it and who helps law enforcement. Requires a certification signed by police or a prosecutor.

paths.name: T visa
paths.plain: For a victim of human trafficking. There is no filing deadline.

paths.name: VAWA
paths.plain: For someone abused by a U.S. citizen or permanent resident spouse, parent, or adult child. They file it themselves, and the abuser is never told.

paths.name: Voluntary departure
paths.plain: Leaving without a removal order on their record, which keeps some future doors open. It has strict deadlines and usually a bond. Nobody should choose this without a lawyer.
